item.title: Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming: Artificial Intelligence for Decision Making in Economic and Social Sciences
item.content:encoded:
Matteo Rocca, University of Insubria

Davide La Torre, Skema Business School

Constantin Zopounidis, Technical University of Crete

This special issue aims to publish selected papers presented during the 16th International Conference on Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming (MOPGP'25) that will be held on 1–3 July 2025, in Varese, Italy. Contributions arising from papers presented at the conference should be substantially extended and cite the conference paper where appropriate. The special issue will also consider papers not presented during the conference. Original and unpublished work not currently under consideration in any other journal is sought.

The intersection of Multiple Objective Optimization (MOP), Goal Programming (GP), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) creates a robust framework for addressing complex decision-making challenges in Economic and Social Sciences. MOP provides structured methods to evaluate and prioritize conflicting objectives, while GP helps setting specific goals to be achieved by the decision maker. AI leverages data analytics and machine learning to process large datasets, revealing insights that improve the accuracy and the robustness of decision models and predictions.

Potential topics

  • Advancements in Multiple Objective Programming Techniques
  • Goal Programming Techniques and Formulations
  • Goal Programming Approaches in Public Policy
  • AI-Enhanced Decision Support Systems for Resource Allocation
  • Data-Driven Methods in Economic and Social Decision-Making
  • Integrating Machine Learning with MOP
  • Multicriteria Deep Learning
  • Applications of MOP and GP in Sustainable Development
  • Real-Time Decision-Making Frameworks Using AI
  • Comparative Studies of MOP and GP in Various Contexts
  • Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis in Sustainable Economics
  • Multiple Criteria Decision Making in Environmental Economics
  • Optimization Models for Social Welfare
  • Behavioural Insights in Multi-Objective Decision-Making
  • Metaheuristics and Computational Methods in MOP
  • MOP and MCDM in AI applications
  • Innovative Applications to Economic and Social Sciences

Timeline

  • June 30, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Data Envelopment Analysis at Fifty: From efficiency measurement to intelligent data-enabled analytics and decision making
item.content:encoded:
This special issue celebrates the 55th anniversary of Omega journal and marks fifty years since the introduction of Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA). The special issue seeks to showcase the evolution of DEA from its origins as a tool for efficiency measurement to its current applications in intelligent data-enabled analytics and decision making.

Timeline

  • May 31, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Extended Reality (XR) for Enhanced Decision Making and Organizational Transformation
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on the transformative potential of Extended Reality (XR) technologies—including Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), and Mixed Reality (MR)—in enhancing decision-making processes and driving organizational transformation. As organizations increasingly face complex challenges requiring rapid, data-driven decisions, XR technologies offer innovative approaches to visualize information, simulate scenarios, and facilitate collaborative problem-solving in immersive environments.

The special issue welcomes original research contributions that explore how XR can improve decision support systems across various organizational contexts. We are interested in studies examining the effectiveness of immersive technologies in enhancing situational awareness, reducing decision-making time, improving decision quality, and fostering organizational innovation. Both theoretical frameworks and practical implementations are encouraged.

Potential topics

  • Applications of XR technologies in decision support systems
  • Immersive visualization for complex data analysis
  • VR/AR/MR interfaces for business intelligence
  • XR-based training and knowledge transfer for organizational learning
  • Human-computer interaction in extended reality environments
  • User experience and usability in XR decision support applications
  • Integration of XR with artificial intelligence and machine learning
  • Real-time collaboration in virtual/mixed reality spaces
  • XR applications in crisis management and emergency response
  • Organizational change management through XR adoption

Timeline

  • January 31, 2027: Full paper submission deadline
